prose.title: Real Deal Creel Spent the Most, Churned the Most, and Leads Its Division on Paper
prose.dek: Keith Creelman spent {{f.team.0008.faa_spend}} at the Free Agent Auction, more than any owner, landed Puka Nacua in the summer's three-way, and made {{f.team.0008.pickups_s3}} waiver pickups before week one. The preseason simulation ranks Real Deal Creel {{f.team.0008.power_rank|ord}}, and first in Maddie Mondays.

paragraphs: April was a teardown. Creelman carried {{f.team.0008.active_roster_opening}} active players, not enough for a lineup, and just {{f.team.0008.cap_opening}} in salary, the smallest commitment in the league. Dallas Goedert was the one top-twelve player and Tetairoa McMillan was solid; the rest, Deshaun Watson, TreVeyon Henderson, Christian Watson, Marvin Harrison Jr., Trey Benson and Keon Coleman, were stopgaps, and Emanuel Wilson's rookie deal was running out.

The first big move came in April, and it was an extend-and-trade: Kenneth Walker, extended a year and then shipped, the largest contract he moved all year at {{f.team.0008.biggest_contract_traded_away}}, went to HammerTime for their 2027 first. The trade bot was not grading deals yet; graded now as of that day, it comes out {{f.team.0008.trade1_grade}} for Real Deal Creel. Blake Watson was released from the taxi squad at no cost. Two rookie deals ran out: Emanuel Wilson went to Blake Bombers at the Expired Rookie Auction and Jalen Carter was let go.

t.0008.slot_bridge.title: April: who held each priced slot

paragraphs: Draft night he made three trades, and the bot graded all three as middling: 1.04 to Gride for 1.07 and Travis Etienne, whom Gride had tagged three days earlier, a {{f.team.0008.trade2_grade}}; 2.09 and a 2027 third to Pure Greatness for 2.06, a {{f.team.0008.trade3_grade}}; and 3.09 and 3.12 to Gride for 3.06, a {{f.team.0008.trade4_grade}}. That last pick had been CBP's, then L.A. Looks', CBP's again, Sex Manther's and The Long Haulers', and Gride had held it for an hour; Creelman used it less than a minute after the trade, on Sonny Styles, who already projects as a High-end LB1. He made {{f.team.0008.rookie_picks_count}} picks in all: KC Concepcion at 1.07, a slot that has produced a usable player more often than not, Omar Cooper Jr. at 1.09, De'Zhaun Stribling, Styles and Zion Young. He was the busiest buyer at the Expired Rookie Auction too, {{f.team.0008.era_lots_won}} players for {{f.team.0008.era_spend}}: Chris Rodriguez, Kayshon Boutte, Michael Mayer, Kendre Miller and Will McDonald.

In July Creelman made room. He cut Noah Fant ({{f.team.0008.cut_14137_salary}} of salary, a {{f.team.0008.cut_14137_penalty}} penalty), Trey Benson ({{f.team.0008.cut_16594_salary}}, {{f.team.0008.cut_16594_penalty}}) and Keon Coleman ({{f.team.0008.cut_16617_salary}}, {{f.team.0008.cut_16617_penalty}}), and in the three-way with C-Town and Blake Bombers he sent McMillan, his own 2027 first, Rodriguez and Omar Cooper for Puka Nacua, an Elite WR1, moving {{f.team.0008.trade5_salary_out}} of salary out and {{f.team.0008.trade5_salary_in}} in, an {{f.team.0008.trade5_grade}} from the bot. The first-round pick he gave up was his own; the one Walker bought, HammerTime's, is still his. He went into the auction with {{f.team.0008.active_roster_preauction}} active players and {{f.team.0008.cap_preauction}} in active-roster salary.

t.0008.moves_s2.title: From the draft to the auction lock

paragraphs: Real Deal Creel spent {{f.team.0008.faa_spend}} at the Free Agent Auction, more than anyone, on {{f.team.0008.faa_lots_won}} players: Dak Prescott for {{f.team.0008.faa_12620_price}} after fifteen bids, Saquon Barkley for {{f.team.0008.faa_13604_price}}, Kyler Murray for {{f.team.0008.faa_14056_price}}, and Jacoby Brissett, Blake's July cut, for {{f.team.0008.faa_12616_price}} as insurance. Hours after winning Prescott, in the middle of the auction, he made more room by back-loading Nacua's deal to {{f.team.0008.rt_16211_salary}} this year and {{f.team.0008.rt_16211_next_salary}} in 2027, freeing {{f.team.0008.restructure_room_freed}}; he put it back as it was {{f.team.0008.rt_16211_days}} days later, four days before the season opened, and the total never changed.

The auction bought Prescott and Barkley, the two Very good buys; Murray, the Good one in the superflex; and Parker Washington, who starts. The league table ranks Real Deal Creel {{f.team.0008.faa_off_rank|ord}} of {{f.league.teams}} for how much the auction improved the offense.

The churn came after the auction: {{f.team.0008.pickups_s3}} waiver pickups before week one, more than anyone, most of them one-for-one swaps at the back of the roster, and Trey Benson among them, claimed back less than three weeks after he was cut. Most of the multi-year contracts came in September. The two big ones were front-loaded: Washington for {{f.team.0008.contract_16192_years}} years at a TCV of {{f.team.0008.contract_16192_tcv}}, {{f.team.0008.contract_16192_salary}} this year, and Chig Okonkwo for {{f.team.0008.contract_15889_years}} at {{f.team.0008.contract_15889_tcv}}, {{f.team.0008.contract_15889_salary}} this year. The rest were small deals: Brian Robinson, Stefon Diggs and, back in July, Cam Little from the auction, the two Expired Rookie Auction buys and {{f.team.0008.myac_other}} waiver pickups. He traded George Karlaftis and a 2027 fifth to the Hawks for their fourth, an {{f.team.0008.trade6_grade}} from the bot, and cut Deshaun Watson with a {{f.team.0008.cut_13113_penalty}} penalty charged to 2027. He sits at {{f.team.0008.cap_current_room}} of room.

The lineup it built has {{f.team.0008.studs_today}} top-twelve starters, Prescott, Barkley, Nacua and Goedert, with Etienne and Murray solid, and {{f.team.0008.holes_today}} holes: Christian Watson at receiver and Washington and Henderson in the flexes. The defense is the soft spot, which is a little awkward for the owner who has added {{f.team.0008.idp_adds_alltime}} defenders since 2010, the most in the league: on MFL's projections only Nick Bolton among the starters grades above replacement level, and Sonny Styles, the rookie who already projects as a High-end LB1, is on the taxi squad.

Henderson is out for the opener with an ankle, so the forecast sits him in week one and Marvin Harrison Jr. is next up in the flex. James Pearce is suspended into November, and Benson, cut and claimed back, is on injured reserve for the season.

captions.t.0008.faa_value: Ranked by how much each owner's starting offense improved between the auction lock and the close; a buy that never makes the lineup adds nothing. What it bought grades each quarterback, back, receiver and tight end at his position: Elite is the top three, Very good the rest of the top twelve, Good the next twelve at quarterback, back and receiver (every team starts two, counting the superflex), Starter anyone else the league's lineups would start, and Depth the rest.

paragraphs: Creelman has been here since {{f.team.0008.hist_first_season}}, all {{f.team.0008.hist_seasons}} completed seasons, and the record has one gap that everyone in the league knows about: {{f.team.0008.hist_playoffs}} playoff trips, {{f.team.0008.hist_div_titles}} division titles, runner-up finishes in 2013 and 2019, and no title. His career all-play record is {{f.team.0008.hist_allplay_pct}}.

He started the Owner Divisional Draft talk in January and then was drafted himself: Josh Martel, the last of the four captains, took Real Deal Creel {{f.league.div_draft_pick_0008|ord}} overall and L.A. Looks right after, rivals on purpose. Maddie Mondays is the closest division in the simulation, and Real Deal Creel leads it: {{f.team.0008.sim_p_division}} to win it, against {{f.league.p_division_0007}} for Sex Manther and {{f.league.p_division_0001}} for L.A. Looks, with {{f.team.0008.sim_p_playoffs}} playoff odds and {{f.team.0008.sim_p_title}} title odds.

The division weeks are {{f.team.0008.div_weeks}}, and week eleven is his hardest, Nacua, Christian Watson and Henderson all on bye. Week eight costs him Etienne and Jonas Sanker. And week fourteen, the last of the regular season, takes Prescott, while L.A. Looks loses three Cowboys and Sex Manther nobody. Across the five weeks he loses {{f.team.0008.div_week_own_byes}} starters to byes, L.A. Looks {{f.team.0008.div_week_byes_0001}} and Sex Manther {{f.team.0008.div_week_byes_0007}}.

the next three years, as the owner would type them.... 2027.... close. manther wins the division and reminds everyone who has the rings haha. 2028.... the division, finally, and the final.... and a third runner-up banner. the commissioner reviews the tape, finds nothing, and shrugs lol. 2029.... he lists the franchise for sale, gets no offers, and keeps it anyway haha

Week one is a division week and has barely started for Real Deal Creel: with {{f.league.wk_teams_final}} NFL teams done, Nacua has scored all {{f.team.0008.wk_points_final}} of the team's points so far, and his week-one waiver claims drew a reply from Josh Martel that none of it is going to be enough.
